subject: general
question: Two circles touch each other internally. How many common tangents can be drawn?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two circles touch **internally**, the smaller circle lies inside the larger one, sharing exactly **one** point on their circumferences.

A common tangent is a line that touches both circles at the same point.

In this configuration, only **one** such line can be drawn at the unique point of contact.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two circles touch each other internally.

**Property:** Let the radii of the two circles be r₁ and r₂ (where r₁ > r₂) and the distance between their centers be d.

⇒ For internal contact, the condition is: d = r₁ − r₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e4b26647f8ccfaa4a2bd304bcd5a8186c290065f63c3ac5601d7de039675d5f6.png] 

⇒ At the point of contact, both circles share a common normal (the line passing through both centers).

⇒ A line perpendicular to this common normal at the point of contact is tangent to both circles.

⇒ Since there is only one point of contact, only **1** common tangent exists.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circles Touching Externally

If d = r₁ + r₂, the circles touch externally and have **3** common tangents (2 direct and 1 transverse).

Circles Intersecting at Two Points

If |r₁ − r₂| r₁ + r₂, the circles are separated and have **4** common tangents (2 direct and 2 transverse).

One Circle Inside Another (No Contact)

If d < |r₁ − r₂|, one circle is completely inside the other without touching, resulting in **0** common tangents.</p
